Treaties are interpreted in good faith under Articles 31–33 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, starting from the ordinary meaning of their terms, read in context and in light of their object and purpose. Supplementary means, such as the preparatory work and the circumstances of conclusion, are used only to confirm that meaning or when the ordinary meaning is ambiguous, obscure, or leads to a manifestly absurd or unreasonable result. The Convention applies to treaties between states, and some states and tribunals treat parts of it as customary law.
CONFIDENCE: 90
